description: Pre-flight check on html / css / js BEFORE writing via update_html. Returns { ok, errors, warnings, parsed } where parsed has byte counts per field and `htmlDropped` (true if the sanitizer would strip anything from `html`) plus `htmlRemoved`, the list of tags (`{ tag, count }`) and attributes (`{ tag, attribute, count }`) it would remove (capped at 25; `htmlRemovedTruncated` flags the cut). The same list appears in the `html_sanitized` warning. Errors cover cap breaches (`html_too_large`, `css_too_large`, `js_too_large`, `total_too_large`) and sanitizer rejection (`html_sanitize_rejected`, `html_sanitize_empty`). The sanitizer keeps `<script>` and `<link>`, but scripts do not run in html surfaces today (inline `<script>` and the `js` field are stored, never executed), so a passing check does not mean script-driven content will work: build static HTML/SVG/CSS. `<canvas>` and `data-*` attributes are kept. Still stripped: any tag or attribute off the allowlist — e.g. `<iframe>`, `<object>`, `<embed>`, `<meta>`, custom elements, inline `on*=` attributes, `javascript:`/`data:text/html` URIs. Read `htmlRemoved` rather than guessing. NEVER writes anything. Use when iterating on a payload so you don't burn a write on something the surface would reject.
name: validate_html
